# Melee Attack

Seven performing a heavy melee attack.

“

Getting close to me was never gonna work out well for ya.

— Bebop

Every hero can perform a **melee attack** to quickly finish off an enemy or do damage while reloading.  Melee damage scales with levels and with certain items like  Melee Lifesteal and  Lifestrike. A light melee attack can be charged up to a heavy melee attack to lunge forward without using up any of the player's Stamina and do more damage; however, the amount a player can turn is reduced during the attack animation. Compared to a normal dash using one Stamina bar, a heavy melee attack lunge travels the player approximately half of the distance. Charging the melee attack can also be done in the air. The default keybind for melee attacks is Q. Pressing Q triggers a light melee attack, while holding initiates a heavy melee attack.

The cooldown for a heavy melee is 1 second, if you miss your heavy melee it will increase to 1.3 seconds.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

See Melee Damage for a list of all heroes' base melee damage and scaling.

Melee attack damage benefits from 50% of all Weapon Damage buffs.

Last hitting a Trooper with a melee attack will prevent its Soul Orb from appearing and give player the full amount of Souls they would have gotten if they shot the Trooper and its orb. Players can perform melee attacks to secure orbs, though they can only do so after a short delay when denying enemy Soul Orbs.

Melee attacks that hit a player climbing an object, such as a ledge or rope, will cause an 80% slowdown that ramps down to 20% over 2 seconds. Melee attacks that hit a player carrying the Soul Urn will force them to drop the urn.

Melee attacks are the only way to interact with the Sinner's Sacrifice and will cause 80 retaliation damage (regardless of whether a Light or Heavy melee was used).

Heavy melee attack is the only way to get the Buffs, claim Rejuvenator or loot the bag of unsecured Souls dropped by a killed hero.

Performing a melee attack will decrease the player's speed shortly after. The amount of speed decreased varies between heroes, and additionally varies depending on if a light or heavy melee is used. The speed decrease can be mitigated through items that give resistance to movement slow effects, such as  Fleetfoot and  Enduring Speed.

Melee attacks will interrupt reloading when performed. Light melee attacks (with the exception of  Billy's) instantly freeze the reload timer on use, while heavy melee attacks will instead freeze the reload timer once the attacking hero begins lunging. Reloading resumes once the melee animation has completed.

## Parry

[edit | edit source]

Parries (Default key: F) are a defensive move that is available to every Hero.

After performing a parry, a Hero briefly enters *a parry state*. The parry animation lasts 1 second, during which any incoming melee attack will be parried for the first 0.75 seconds. During the *parry state*, the player can fully absorb melee attacks and apply the following status effects to the melee attackers: stunning the attacker for 2.75 seconds (cannot be reduced by debuff resistance), preventing incoming melee damage, and making the attacker susceptible to increased damage in return (+25% to all damage sources, not just the individual who parried).

A successful parry has a brief 0.3 second window exiting the parry animation in which the player will not be able to perform anything, after which any action (including another parry) can be performed. Holding the parry key allows the player to parry multiple heroes. An unsuccessful parry has a cooldown of 4.5 seconds before another parry can be performed again.

Debuff Resist does not impact the duration of those status effects from being parried. However,  Unstoppable (and abilities that grant the same effect) does prevent being stunned by a successful parry.

Counterspell and  Rebuttal give additional effects to parries, with Rebuttal also decreasing parry cooldown to 2.5 seconds.

You can parry Troopers (blocks damage but doesn't stun them) and Guardians (blocks damage and prevents them from attacking for a short period; parried Guardian will not attempt another melee attack for a short while). You cannot normally parry Walkers or most abilities, with an exception of  Viscous'  Puddle Punch.

## Heavy Melee Cancel

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Heavy Melee Cancel

**Heavy Melee Cancel** is a technique that allows you to interrupt a Heavy Melee attack by using specific Active Items or Abilities. This is particularly useful for melee-focused builds, as it can bait enemies into wasting their Parry.

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Heavy_Melee_Cancel.mp4**Baiting Heavy Melee by canceling it with  Fleetfoot.**

# Melee Damage

Melee Damage is a stat that Heroes start with and determines how much damage a hero's Melee Attack deals. Melee damage scales with Boons and Items. Melee damage scales with the Weapon Damage stat at a rate of 50%.

Most heroes have the same base melee damage and scaling, with a few exceptions (see table below).

# Melee Distance

**Melee Distance** is a stat that affects how far the player will travel when attacking with melee.

While charging up a Heavy Melee, the player will move forward in a straight line. Turning the mouse allows the character to turn around walls or redirect around parrying enemies.

**Melee Lifesteal** is a Tier 1  Vitality Item that can be purchased from the Shop for  **800**.

It is a component of  Lifestrike.

## Notes

[edit | edit source]

- Metal Skin does *not* provide Bullet Evasion. It blocks Weapon Damage, but on-bullet-hit effects and Build-Ups such as  Haze's  Fixation,  Mirage's  Djinn's Mark or  Slowing Bullets are still applied.
- Metal Skin blocks the damage of any abilities that deal Weapon Damage such as  Venator's  Consecrating Grenade,  Gutshot and  Ira Domini (not counting the Pure Damage effects).
- Metal Skin does not block  Paradox's  Kinetic Carbine, since it deals Spirit Damage.

# Mid-Boss

**Mid-Boss**, also known as the **Mid Boss**, **The Boss** or **Temple Guardian***,* is a powerful neutral jungle boss with strong attacks and a regenerating shield to defend itself. Teams of Heroes may attempt to kill Mid-Boss which immediately grants permanent stats for the team that defeats it, as well as an opportunity to obtain **Rejuvenator Credits**, allowing heroes to revive upon death.

https://deadlock.wiki/File:Midboss_arrive.mp3Mid-Boss spawn SFX

## Contents

- 1 Overview

- 1.1 Health Scaling
- 2 Death

- 2.1 Rejuvenator Credit
- 3 Respawn
- 4 Update history
- 5 Trivia

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

After **10** minutes have elapsed in a match, the Mid-Boss will spawn underground in the sewers in the center of the map. Its arrival is announced through a loud roar, followed by the Patron's announcement, *"The Mid-Boss has arrived"*. While Mid-Boss is alive, a golden Rejuvenator symbol will appear at its location in the minimap.

The path to the Mid-Boss' pit can be found in entrances marked with the Rejuvenator sign, at the Blue lane. These entrances will also have a glowing Rejuvenator symbol above them when the Mid-Boss has respawned.

The Mid-Boss is initially dormant and will not attack anyone outside its pit. As soon as a player has entered the pit, the Mid-Boss will attack by channeling a bright purple beam onto them, dealing Weapon Damage. If multiple players are inside the pit, it will prioritize the closest one. Additionally, the Mid-Boss can only be damaged by players who are inside its pit, and will be completely invulnerable to outside attacks.

Unlike most units, Mid-Boss has a special shield surrounding it at all times that prevents it from taking health damage. In order to actually harm it, enough damage needs to be dealt to deplete the constantly regenerating shield, which can prove difficult for individual or unprepared players. The damage shield starts at **35** HP and increases at **5** HP/minute (85 HP when the Mid-Boss first spawns).

Once Mid-Boss has reached 50% Health, it will roar once again, announcing to both teams that it is close to death.

### Health Scaling

[edit | edit source]

Mid-Boss' Health scales linearly from when it spawns. For every minute that passes after it has spawned, it gains an additional **195** Health, which is added to its **13000** Base Health.

## Death

[edit | edit source]

When the Mid-Boss is slain, the killing team gains  **3000** souls, 2 Golden Statue buffs per player and a Rejuvenator crystal spawns above the pit to begin its slow descent, which takes 6 seconds. The Rejuvenator crystal is not targetable as it descends and cannot be claimed until it has fully landed on the ground. Once landed, attacking it with a heavy melee attack grants a **Rejuvenator Credit** to the entire team. Each heavy melee hit on the crystal grants one credit, up to 3 for each Mid-Boss kill. The first credit claimed will also grant a 100% heal to the hero. Either team may take rejuvenator credits regardless of which team kills the Mid-Boss, allowing for players to steal rejuvenators after the Mid-Boss has been slain.

### Rejuvenator Credit

[edit | edit source]

Main article: Rejuvenator

The Rejuvenator credit grants all team members a buff that allows them to revive with **100%** health in the place of their death after 3s. When a player dies, they respawn in place, lose the buff, and their team’s Rejuvenator credits are reduced by 1 (each player can consume only one credit).

The Rejuvenator credit lasts 4 minutes. The top UI bar displays the remaining Rejuvenator credits. Once all credits are used, the buff is removed from all team members.

## Respawn

[edit | edit source]

The Mid-Boss respawns **7** minutes after its first death. Then it respawns 6 minutes after its second death, and 5 minutes after its third and subsequent deaths.

A timer until the Mid-Boss respawn can be seen as its icon fills up in the minimap. Pressing Tab shows players the exact time in minutes/seconds.

“

They die, when I say they die.

**Mina** is a Hero in *Deadlock*; a glass cannon that delivers quick bursts of Spirit damage at range with her passive, Love Bites. She can transform into bats and escape when things get a bit too messy. Each time she triggers Love Bites, her vampiric powers grow stronger. This builds toward her ultimate, Nox Nostra, which unleashes a massive swarm of bats that hunt down and silence nearby enemies.

Mina Ha was an ambitious and rich girl betrothed to American royalty, the eldest heir to the Fairfax Industries fortune. However, her hopes were dashed when her fiancé was assassinated prior to the wedding. Her parents, seeking only the best for their daughter, contracted a vampire to turn Mina into a vampire and grant her eternal life. Now learning her new powers and navigating vampire high society, Mina's ambitious eye is set on becoming the next Viscount of New York.

Mina was released on August 18, 2025 as the first hero in the Six New Heroes update.

## Backstory

[edit | edit source]

*See **Mina/Lore** for more story content.*

“

Mina Ha had it all...rich parents, elite education, and an arranged marriage that would see her ascend from run-of-the-mill upper class to American royalty.  She was happy.

Then her betrothed was assassinated.

Mina wept; not for the life of her fiancé, but for the future that was stolen from her.  Why couldn’t the killer just wait until after the wedding? Then she’d have the last name she always dreamed of and no one would even have to pretend to love anyone.  It could have been perfect, but life wasn’t fair...and so Mina did what she always does when things don’t go her way: she told her parents to fix it.

Mr. And Mrs. Ha knew that the only way to appease their daughter was to offer her something greater than what she lost... and marrying into one of the world’s most lauded families was a tall order to top.  They had to think big.  They had to think outside of the box.  They had to promise their daughter immortality.

It took a small fortune, but eventually they found a vampire who was willing to turn her.  Unsurprisingly, Mina thought the idea of eternal youth and a trust fund was an acceptable plan B and happily agreed to the proposal.  Now a fledgling vampire, Mina is quickly discovering that the clout she held as a human has no weight in vampire high society...and while at first that annoyed her, if there is one thing Mina has a knack for, it's learning the rules so she can subvert them.  She will be the Viscount of New York, the other vampires just don't know it yet.

## Trivia

[edit | edit source]

- Mina is named after the literary character Mina Harker, from Bram Stoker's *Dracula*.
- Mina's ultimate Nox Nostra means "Our Night" in Latin.
- Mina is the second hero to use "vampire" as a codename (VampireBat), as there is another hero referenced in the localization files as "hero_vampire", but it has been removed from the game.
- Mina's name is written in the Korean and Simplified Chinese localizations with the last name before the first name, unlike other heroes. "Ha" is a traditional East Asian last name.
- Mina was one of the heroes in a private build who was accidently leaked on stream in May 2025.[3] Mina's model was leaked by an anonymous source along with a WIP version of the shop UI, ahead of the Shop Rework update.
- Mina's pistol New Money has the words "Nuit Rouge 7" ("Red Night 7" in French) inscribed on the side, not seen in the weapon art.
- "Grabbing a bite in the Hideout" is displayed as one's status in the in-game Friends List when playing as Mina in the Hideout.
- Mina holds her pistol in her left hand, like  Lady Geist.

## Overview

[edit | edit source]

Mina's motivation in the ritual is to become Viscount of New York.[1]

### Biography

[edit | edit source]

Mina graduated from Blackmore Academy.[2]

Mina's fiancé was  Pocket,[3][4][5] who suffered an assassination attempt by  Calico 5 years before the events of the game.[6][7]

Mina is a fashion designer and owns a clothing brand.[8][9] She knows how to sew.[10]

### Personality

[edit | edit source]

Mina is generally antagonistic to most other characters.[11] According to  Vindicta, Mina has a reputation for being unpleasant.[12]

### Information

[edit | edit source]

Mina complains that her parents "botched" her turning into a vampire.[13]

## Character Relationships

[edit | edit source]

### Pocket

[edit | edit source]

As mentioned in the biography, Mina's fiancé was Pocket.[3][4][5]

Mina hates Pocket for "ruining her life", as Pocket's assassination meant Mina couldn't become a Fairfax.[14][15]

### Lady Geist

[edit | edit source]

Mina idolises Lady Geist,[16][17] who believes Mina has "potential".[18] Mina wants to dress Geist for the Met Gala.[19]

### Infernus

[edit | edit source]

Mina got carded at Jezebel's by Infernus on her 16th birthday and attempted to bribe him to let her stay.[20][21]

-Mina's parents

## Character Interactions

[edit | edit source]

- Mina idolises Lady Geist,[16][17] who believes Mina has "potential".[18] Mina wants to dress Geist for the Met Gala.[19]
- Mina offers to stitch up Victor's wounds if he models at one of her shows.[22]
- Mina is terrified of Drifter.[23][24] Drifter thinks Mina is a "pathetic excuse for a vampire".[25]
- Mina thinks Billy might have rabies.[26]
- As a fashion designer, Mina dislikes Abrams' coat,[27] Dynamo's jacket,[28] The Doorman's hat,[29] Vindicta's outfit,[30] and calls Paige a "walking fashion crime".[31] She does, however, like Haze's uniform and tie,[32][33] Holliday's hat,[34] Lady Geist's everything,[35]Victor's leather pants[36] and Wraith's hat.[37]
- Mina knows someone named Sandra who thinks Lash is hot.[38]
- Mo & Krill allegedly sold knock-offs of Mina's dresses.[39] Krill thinks Mina's fashion line is "overwrought".[40]
